chapter: On the road and into brass bands
title: Backing the Famous Flames and Little Richard, and why he quit
summary: On a Milt Shaw tour his band backed James Brown and Little Richard; he quit over makeup and dress while Charles Connors and Wilbert Smith stayed.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: George. Oh. What the hell was George's name? Anyhow. His professional name was Papa Lightfoot. His real name was George something. I can't remember now. Anyhow. So we traveled like that for quite some time with Senegal and so forth. Then the band changed up. We started doing some gigs for Milt Shaw. With D. Clark. And we were doing it in Atlanta, Georgia. And Columbus, Georgia. And where we started at that time. We were working around Air Force bases and so forth. Biloxi and all that kind of stuff. With rhythm and blues shows. And I remember we went to Macon, Georgia. So we were supposed to play with this band. Well, we did. We had a band called Fat Man Jackson. And he had a group called the Famous Flames. And they were just getting organized. And we joined the band. We joined Senegal. Edwin Mayer. Eddie Bull. Wilbert Smith. Charles Connors. And myself. We joined that band. To play behind the Famous Flames. With the lead singer was James Brown. And the person who was in the head of the show. The top of the show. Was Richard Pennyworth. Yeah. Pennyworth. Yeah. You know what I'm saying? Little Richard. Little Richard. So. We worked a couple of gigs around the area. And then Little Richard had some kind of a meeting or something. Because he, at the time, was going to be buying suits for the band. And the band had to put on makeup. Lipstick. And straighten their hair up. And all that kind of stuff. Again, my reflections go back to the beginning. When I was going to be called a sissy for playing the violin and the piano. I'm gone.

I'm gone. Here it is. I left. The guitar player, Edwin Mayer, left. Eddie Bull left. Bill Senegal left. And I'm thinking that one. I think Nat left, too. With us. I know he didn't stay. But Charles Connors and Wilbur Smith stayed on with Little Richard. And he made a beautiful career. He made a lot of money with him and so forth and so on. As a matter of fact, Charles still lives in Los Angeles now. Because at one time, even Charles Connors married Little Richard's sister. Wilbur Smith stayed on for a long time and then went on to New York where he lived. Well, Wilbur actually, him and I, we played in the band even before that. But reflecting, go back a little bit, is when Wilbur met a girl from Merida, Mississippi. I met a girl from Nashville, Mississippi. And later on, this girl's daughter turns out to be my daughter-in-law. And Ruby's son turns out to be his wife. I mean, her husband. So now, up until today, Wilbur's grandchildren are mine. We have the same grandchildren. Wilbur is dead now, but Wilbur composed Tell It Like It Is with George Davis and so forth.
Okay, he's working on the name Lee Diamond.
Yeah, Lee Diamond was his professional name.
